dublinCore.description: A sinusoid of N samples is multiplied by a rectangular, Hamming, Hanning, Blackman or Kaiser window and transformed. The spectrum shows the DFT bins on top of the underlying DTFT, with the main-lobe width, peak side-lobe level, scalloping loss and coherent gain measured from the window's own transform.
relation: Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

topic: Spectral leakage and the resolution versus side-lobe trade-off of window functions
learningObjectives: Explain spectral leakage as a consequence of observing a signal for a finite time
Predict whether a tone will leak from its frequency and the bin spacing
Compare windows by main-lobe width, peak side-lobe level and scalloping loss
Choose a window for resolving two close tones or for finding a weak tone near a strong one
prerequisites: Multiplication in time as convolution in frequency

misconceptions.misconception: Leakage is a numerical error of the FFT
misconceptions.correction: Leakage is exact mathematics: a finite record is the signal times a window, so its spectrum is the true spectrum convolved with the window's transform
misconceptions.evidence: The grey DTFT curve shows the same spread that the FFT bins sample, and a bin-centred tone with the rectangular window shows no leakage at all

misconceptions.misconception: A tapered window always gives a better spectrum than the rectangular window
misconceptions.correction: Tapering lowers the side lobes but widens the main lobe, and a bin-centred tone is cleanest with no window at all
misconceptions.evidence: With the tone on a bin centre the rectangular window shows one dot while Hanning shows three and Blackman five; with two tones 6 Hz apart at N = 256 only the rectangular window shows a clear dip

misconceptions.misconception: Zero-padding or a longer FFT lowers the side lobes of a window
misconceptions.correction: The peak side-lobe level depends only on the window shape; a longer record narrows the main lobe in hertz
misconceptions.evidence: Change FFT size N and the peak side-lobe readout does not move

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Four plots: a sinusoid of N samples, the window function, the windowed signal and its magnitude spectrum in decibels. Dots mark the DFT bins on the continuous spectrum, with the main-lobe width and peak side-lobe level of the window marked. A banner says whether the tone lies on a bin centre.

controls.label: Signal
controls.description: Chooses a single sinusoid, two close sinusoids 6 Hz apart, or a strong sinusoid with a weak one 24 Hz above and 40 dB below

controls.label: Window
controls.description: Chooses the window applied to the N samples before the transform

controls.label: FFT size N
controls.description: Number of samples in the record; the bin spacing is fs/N

controls.label: Frequency f (Hz)
controls.description: Frequency of the (first) sinusoid, shown with its position in bins

controls.label: Bin centre
controls.description: Moves the tone to the nearest bin centre

controls.label: Half-way
controls.description: Moves the tone to the nearest point half-way between two bins

controls.label: Kaiser β
controls.description: Shape parameter of the Kaiser window; enabled only when the Kaiser window is selected

visualElements.description: Time signal x[n], window w[n] and windowed signal x[n] w[n] as three stacked plots
Magnitude spectrum in dB: DFT bins as dots on the DTFT curve, with the shaded main lobe, the dashed peak side-lobe level, the true tone frequencies and a mouse cursor readout
Banner telling whether the tone is on a bin centre, and a table of measured window properties

model.description: N samples of one or two sinusoids at fs = 1024 Hz are multiplied by a window and transformed with a radix-2 FFT; the DTFT curve is an 8x zero-padded FFT, and window properties are measured from a 512-point window zero-padded 64 times
equations: X[k] = sum over n of x[n] w[n] e^(-j 2 pi k n / N), bin spacing = fs / N
Hanning: w[n] = 0.5 - 0.5 cos(2 pi n / N); Hamming: w[n] = 0.54 - 0.46 cos(2 pi n / N)
Blackman: w[n] = 0.42 - 0.5 cos(2 pi n / N) + 0.08 cos(4 pi n / N)
assumptions: fs = 1024 Hz; the second close tone is 6 Hz above the first; the weak tone is 24 Hz above and 40 dB below the strong one
The DTFT curve is an 8x zero-padded FFT of the windowed signal
Window properties are measured on a 512-point window zero-padded 64 times
The signal is a real sinusoid, so leakage from its negative-frequency image is included

instructionalStrategies: Predict whether a tone will leak, test it, then compare windows on measured properties
Tabulate main-lobe width and peak side-lobe level for the four fixed windows
Decide which windows reveal a tone 40 dB below a strong neighbour
extensions: Find the Kaiser beta that matches the side lobes of Hamming and Blackman and compare main-lobe widths
